estimates.assumptions: Standard medium green chili pepper is ~15g when chopped; matches known cal density for fresh chili.
Typical fresh coriander (cilantro) bunch used in recipes is 20-30g edible leaves and stalks; using 25g here as modest amount for stir-fry.
Average lime yields ~30g (2 tbsp) juice; using juice-only edible portion with given cal density for lime juice.
1 tbsp oil = 14g so 2 tbsp = 28g; matches known high cal density for groundnut/peanut oil.
3cm piece of ginger root weighs ~9g when peeled/sliced for stir-fry; matches known cal density for fresh ginger.
8 spring onions (scallions) sliced is ~60g total edible portion; matches known cal density for fresh spring onions.
1 medium red bell pepper sliced is ~120g edible flesh; matches known cal density for raw red pepper.
Measurement already supplies 85g; using typical cal density for canned water chestnuts (drained, ~50 kcal/100g).
'To serve' with no quantity; cannot reasonably estimate total dry noodle grams for the whole recipe without inventing a serving count.
